nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of α-Co(OH)₂
nodes.procedure: A small amount of hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) was introduced during the hydrothermal process to prepare α-Co(OH)₂ possessing a layered crystal structure with interlayer anion of NO₃⁻, which exhibited a three-dimensional nanosheet array morphology on carbon cloth.

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal synthesis
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: a small amount of hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) was introduced during the hydrothermal process

nodes.source_text: Typically, α-Co(OH)₂ possesses a layered crystal structure with interlayer anion of NO₃⁻ and a small amount of hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) was introduced during the hydrothermal process in our experiment (Figure 1a). The as-prepared sample exhibited a three-dimensional nanosheet array morphology on carbon cloth (Figure 1b)

nodes.name: Electrolyte modification with MoO₄²⁻
nodes.procedure: Addition of 0.1 M MoO₄²⁻ (from sodium molybdate) to 1 M KOH electrolyte results in MoO₄²⁻ riveting on the surface of α-Co(OH)₂, stabilizing oxygen vacancies and modulating electronic structure.

unit_operations.name: Electrolyte preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: adding 0.1 M MoO₄²⁻ to 1 M KOH

unit_operations.name: Surface modification
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: MoO₄²⁻ riveted on the surface of α-Co(OH)₂

nodes.source_text: the best performance was obtained by adding 0.1 M MoO₄²⁻... MoO₄²⁻ can be riveted on the surface of α-Co(OH)₂

nodes.name: Electrolyte modification with WO₄²⁻
nodes.procedure: Addition of WO₄²⁻ (from sodium tungstate) to 1 M KOH electrolyte exhibits similar protective effect on α-Co(OH)₂ structure and morphology as MoO₄²⁻.

unit_operations.name: Electrolyte preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: addition of WO₄²⁻ with similar structure

nodes.characterization_summary: Hexagonal structure confirmed by powder XRD patterns (Figure S1). The (003) peak at 9.3° decreases sharply after 50 LSV scans and disappears after 300 scans in 1 M KOH, but remains nearly unchanged with MoO₄²⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: hexagonal structure confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure S1, Supporting Information)... the intensity of the peak corresponding to the (003) plane of α-Co(OH)₂ at 9.3° decreased sharply after 50 LSV scans

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 440 and 487 cm⁻¹ assigned to α-Co(OH)₂ decrease and vanish after 300 LSV scans in 1 M KOH, but remain stable with MoO₄²⁻ addition. New peak at 890 cm⁻¹ assigned to MoO₄ tetrahedron stretching vibration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peaks assigned to α-Co(OH)₂ in Raman (two peaks at 440 and 487 cm⁻¹) ... decreased gradually and vanished after 300 LSV scans... one new peak at 890 cm⁻¹ in the Raman spectrum... assigned to stretching vibration of MoO₄ tetrahedron.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows peaks at 500 and 628 cm⁻¹ for α-Co(OH)₂ and 1010, 1195, 1342 cm⁻¹ for HMT. New peak at 850 cm⁻¹ for MoO₄²⁻ tetrahedron stretching after addition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similarly, the peaks assigned to α-Co(OH)₂ in Raman (two peaks at 440 and 487 cm⁻¹) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR, the peaks at 500 and 628 cm⁻¹ corresponding to α-Co(OH)₂ ; the peaks at 1010, 1195, and 1342 cm⁻¹ corresponding to HMT molecular)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows three-dimensional nanosheet array morphology on carbon cloth, preserved after 300 LSV scans with MoO₄²⁻ but transforms to nanoparticles in pure KOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-prepared sample exhibited a three-dimensional nanosheet array morphology on carbon cloth (Figure 1b)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms ultrathin nanosheets remain intact after 300 LSV scans with MoO₄²⁻ addition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image (Figure S16, Supporting Information) shows that the ultrathin nanosheets remain intact after 300 LSV scans

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p₃/₂ at 781.4 eV and Co 2p₁/₂ at 797.4 eV with satellites at 786.5 and 803.2 eV. After 50 LSV in KOH, Co 2p₃/₂ shifts to 781.1 eV (-0.3 eV); mitigated to -0.15 eV with MoO₄²⁻. O 1s: 531.3 eV (hydroxide), 532.3 eV (Ov), 533.4 eV (adsorbed water); Ov peak disappears in KOH but stable with MoO₄²⁻. Mo 3d: 231.9 and 235.0 eV (Mo⁶⁺).
nodes.evidence_snippet: for Co 2p, the two peaks at 781.4 and 797.4 eV can be ascribed to Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂ of α-Co(OH)₂ with two satellite peaks at 786.5 and 803.2 eV... after the measurements in 1 m KOH, the peak of Co 2p₃/₂ at 781.1 eV was negatively shifted by 0.3 eV... Mo 3d (Figure 2c), two peaks at 231.9 and 235.0 eV can be well attributed to Mo⁶⁺ from MoO₄²⁻

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows strong signal at g=2.003 for oxygen vacancies in initial α-Co(OH)₂, disappears after HER in KOH but remains stable with narrower halfwidth with MoO₄²⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2d, a strong signal at the g value of 2.003 was clearly observed in the initial α-Co(OH)₂, however, which almost disappeared after HER in 1 m KOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX shows homogeneous distribution of Co, Mo, O elements with low Mo content of 0.21%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping images (Figures S30c and S31c, Supporting Information) indicate the homogeneous distribution of Co, Mo, and O elements within nanosheets, and the low content of Mo element (0.21%)

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl from CV at different scan rates gives ECSA values increasing from 6.5 mF cm⁻² (1 M KOH) to 8.1 mF cm⁻² (with MoO₄²⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical surface area (ECSA) values calculated from the corresponding electrochemical double layer capacitance (Cdl) obtained from the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves at different scan rates increases slightly (from 6.5 to 8.1 mF cm⁻², Figures S26b and S27, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS indicates charge transfer process accelerated by MoO₄²⁻ addition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) indicates that the charge transfer process was effectively accelerated by the MoO₄²⁻ addition (Figure S26d, Supporting Information).
